headline: High risk of filesystem-based prompt injection and data leakage; Dify’s shared datastore plus Claude Code’s broad host access create dangerous default pairings.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads and writes repo files and can use MCP; Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge base files and tool outputs. That creates a plausible path where content from one agent is treated as instructions by the other, especially through shared filesystem artifacts or workflow inputs. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Claude Code writes attacker-controlled text into a repo file that Dify later ingests as knowledge base content, injection is possible.
IF Dify forwards untrusted tool output into a workflow that Claude Code later parses as instructions, injection is possible.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces.
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files into Dify knowledge bases.
Add a manual review step before Claude Code consumes Dify-generated text.
Use provenance tags on all inter-agent artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, while Dify handles knowledge base content, conversation logs, model-provider keys, and tool credentials. Because Claude Code shares state via filesystem and git, and Dify stores conversation data server-side, the pair can move sensitive material across boundaries in default workflows. The blast radius includes secrets and code exfiltration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Claude Code is pointed at a repository containing secrets or credentials, those may enter its context.
IF Dify workflows ingest those artifacts into conversation logs or knowledge base content, sensitive data is retained and redistributed.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running either agent.
Store credentials in a separate secret manager, not in files.
Restrict Dify knowledge-base uploads to scrubbed documents only.
Rotate any credentials that may already have been exposed.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on inter-agent file transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and execute shell commands, and Claude Code also modifies git state while Dify uses a shared server datastore. If they operate on the same repository or mutable workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt files or git history without coordination. The profiles show no locking primitive between them, so the conflict is a dangerous default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents target the same working directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF Claude Code commits while Dify writes generated artifacts into the same repo, git state can diverge or be corrupted.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate directory.
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file.
Disable git writes from Claude Code during Dify runs.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an agent/orchestration platform that wires tools into workflows, while Claude Code produces code and shell actions. If Dify treats Claude Code output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream tool calls or workflow actions without verification. Because the pair is designed for agentic chaining, the default blast radius can include incorrect commits or operational actions.
conditions: IF Dify consumes Claude Code output without a validation step, downstream actions may execute incorrect instructions.
IF Claude Code emits fabricated facts or commands into a Dify workflow, those can be propagated to tools.
mitigations: Insert a human approval gate before any action step.
Require schema validation on Claude Code outputs.
Limit Dify workflows to read-only actions until tested.
Log and diff intermediate outputs before execution.
requires-engineering: add verifier agents or policy checks between the two systems.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code runs on the invoking user’s host and handles git credentials and shell environment, while Dify stores conversation logs and knowledge-base content on its server. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch for the same data class when the pair is used together. The profiles do not specify a concrete regulatory regime, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Claude Code and then mirrored into Dify logs or knowledge bases, retention obligations may diverge.
IF the deployment spans jurisdictions with different residency rules, stored conversation logs may violate policy.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts.
Set short retention on Dify conversation logs.
Document which data classes may enter each system.
Purge old logs and uploaded files regularly.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both platforms.
